newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia opens key Adriatic highway bridge.
newsitem.headline: Croatia opens key Adriatic highway bridge.

text.p: Croatia opened a major highway bridge on the scenic Adriatic coast on Monday to replace one blown up by Serb rebels in 1991.
The 377-metre (1,244-foot) Maslenica bridge near Zadar opened for traffic at midday (1100 GMT). An official state ceremony will take place later this week.

HINA, the official news agency, said the reinforced concrete bridge was the 15th longest of its kind. State road company Hrvatske Ceste invested 80 million kuna ($13 million) in the project which took four years to complete.
The bridge lies on the shortest route between industrial centres in north Croatia, including the capital Zagreb, and the Dalmatian coast in the south -- the centre of the country's tourist industry.
It spans a rocky gorge close to the ruins of the old Maslenica bridge bombed by separatist minority Serbs in the closing stages of Croatia's 1991 war for independence from what was then Yugoslavia.

The Maslenica gorge, 20 km (12 miles) north of Zadar, was the scene of vicious battles in January 1993 when Croatian troops broke U.N. ceasefire lines to push back rebel Serbs to free up the region for traffic.

Six months later President Franjo Tudjman opened a makeshift pontoon bridge which until Monday served as the only coastal link between north and south apart from the damaged Pag island bridge which required a major detour and a ferry trip.
